subject: Clarify dataflow, subprocessor notify & breach-notify expectations
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: anna.kaufmann@medsync.io
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up — data handling clarifications

Hi Anna — thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can scope the DPA/implementation work: 

- What we heard (high level): ClearHealth will send model inputs that include limited PII (patient initials, hashed identifiers, short clinical notes snippets). Processing will occur for inference only; ClearHealth will persist logs for troubleshooting/traceability. You indicated a preference for US residency for logs and model execution for HIPAA alignment.

- Open questions we need to confirm to proceed with a draft DPA addendum and SOW: 
  1) Controller vs processor mapping: Please confirm whether ClearHealth is the controller for the inputs and whether Redwood will be an exclusive processor for inference and ephemeral cacheing only.
  2) Subprocessor notifications: what internal SLA/notify window do you require before you expect subprocessor changes to be communicated? (e.g., 30 days / 14 days / immediate for high-risk changes)
  3) Breach notification timing: You mentioned a 72-hour internal target — is that the contractual requirement you need?
  4) Retention & logs: typical Redwood defaults are 30 days of request logs + 90 days of aggregated metrics unless configured otherwise. Do you need longer retention for audit evidence?
  5) Evidence & auditability: Do you require SOC 2 Type II artifacts or on-demand copies of access logs / split-key encryption proof?

Attachments: I don't have your dataflow diagram — could you send the high-level dataflow and any existing DPA language you prefer? I will loop in Marissa (privacy/legal) to annotate our standard DPA for your review.

Next steps: if you can reply with the dataflow and answers above, Ben and I will produce an annotated DPA and a short mutual action plan (timeline + owners). Happy to set a 30-minute follow-up if you prefer to walk through the diagram.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Anna Kaufmann <anna.kaufmann@medsync.io>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: security@medsync.io
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — data handling clarifications

Thanks Jasmine — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Controller/processor: ClearHealth will remain Controller for patient data. We expect Redwood to be Processor for inference and for any transient KV/prefix caching. We cannot accept any secondary use of data for model training.

- Subprocessor notifications: for anything that changes hosting location or involves a new vendor with access to plaintext inputs, we require 14 days notice and an opportunity to review the subprocessor contract. For lower-risk operational subprocessors (e.g., monitoring vendor with no data access), 30 days is acceptable.

- Breach notify: We need contract language that Redwood will notify ClearHealth within 48 hours of becoming aware of an incident that reasonably affects our data. We will coordinate public disclosure timelines together.

- Retention & logs: We need request-level logs retained for 180 days for our auditors (IP, timestamp, request ID, redacted payload hash). We are flexible on aggregated metrics.

- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report is required prior to signing; additionally we will want 12 months of historical access logs accessible on request.

Attached: MedSync-Dataflow-Diagram.pdf (high-level)

If you can produce an annotated DPA that reflects these asks and call out any items Redwood cannot accommodate, we can review internally and get Legal engaged.

Best,
Anna Kaufmann
Head of Product & Privacy (acting)
ClearHealth Analytics
anna.kaufmann@medsync.io
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: anna.kaufmann@medsync.io, jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo follow-up — data handling clarifications

Hi Anna / Jasmine — looping in legal/ privacy. Per our internal standards, a few initial notes: 

1) Training prohibition: Redwood will include a strict no-training clause for customer data unless explicitly agreed; we will commit to process-only usage for ClearHealth.

2) Subprocessor change windows: We can offer a 14-day notice for high-risk subprocessors (those with access to plaintext) and 30 days for lower-risk ops suppliers. We will include an escalation path for emergency changes with immediate notice and compensating controls.

3) Breach notification: Our standard is 72 hours; we can accept 48 hours for incidents where customer data is reasonably likely to have been exfiltrated, subject to coordinated investigation timelines. We will add language about collaboration on regulator notifications.

4) Retention & logs: We can extend request-level logs retention to 180 days for an additional retention add-on (one-time configuration and storage surcharge). We will document field-level redaction and hash-only storage of payloads where feasible.

5) SOC 2: We can provide a SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA; production onboarding requires receipt of that artifact.

I attached an initial annotated DPA (DPA_annotated_v1.pdf) that maps ClearHealth asks to proposed contract language and indicates items that will carry cost or require product configuration.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: anna.kaufmann@medsync.io
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — data handling clarifications

  • Annotated DPA (Marissa) — includes 48/72 hr breach language options called out and a retention add-on section. (attachment: DPA_annotated_v1.pdf)
  • Cost estimate for 180-day log retention and S3 bucket residency in us-west-2 (Ben)
  • Mutual action plan doc with owners + target sign date (drive link below)

- Proposed action plan (high level):
  1) We (Redwood) send updated annotated DPA and cost estimate — 2027-04-21

  3) Final negotiation & DocuSign — target week of 2027-05-03
